copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Spain v Cabo Verde in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Monday, and the model and the market disagree on the the draw side by +3.6pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Spain 470 points higher than the other side (Spain 2010, Cabo Verde 1540). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Spain to win at 84%, the draw at 10%, and Cabo Verde to win at 6%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Spain to win at 89%, the draw at 6%, and Cabo Verde to win at 5%. The the draw side trades at 6% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +1462. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 10%, +3.6pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On the draw, that haircut lands the model at 10%; the market is at 6%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +3.6pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 25 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +3.6pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Spain are a justifiably popular pick as the reigning European champions have plenty of world-class talent.

copy.summary: This is one of the few matches where the model leans toward the draw more than Polymarket does. The model rates the draw at 10%, the market at 6% — a +3.6pp gap.
copy.title: Spain v Cabo Verde · the model leans the draw
